newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: World Bank offers aid for Argentine reforms-report.
newsitem.headline: World Bank offers aid for Argentine reforms-report.

text.p: The World Bank's local representative on Thursday offered Argentina financial aid to help ease the implementation of labor law reform, the state news agency Telam reported.

"The World Bank is willing to help advance the process of labor reform with knowledge and financial aid, above all in this transition phase," Telam quoted Patricio Millan as saying. "We are convinced that labor modernization is an absolute necessity in Argentina, and to that end we can finance some projects."
The official did not quantify the bank's aid.
He said often in Latin America countries used minimum wages, high severance payments and collective bargaining "as a mechanism to reduce the inequality of the distribution of income."
The Argentine government has introduced in Congress proposed reforms that would scrap collective bargaining and make workers' hours and conditions more flexible.
